Role Summary:
Sony Interactive Entertainment’s Legal, Public Policy & ESG team is looking for an experienced lawyer to join its award-winning IP Enforcement practice. This role combines sophisticated and technically complex copyright and content protection work with online and offline enforcement, addressing evolving issues such as piracy, pre-release leaks, game modifications, circumvention, emulators, and other emerging threats affecting PlayStation games and content. As
Corporate Counsel, IP Enforcement
, you will serve as the primary legal contact for IP enforcement in the Americas, with a particular focus on supporting PlayStation Studios and SIE’s Game Protection Program,
our dedicated initiative to combat piracy, protect pre-release content, and address unauthorized game modification.
Reporting to the Director, Global IP Enforcement in the UK, you will work closely with legal, technical, investigative, security, fraud, and business teams around the world. This is a highly collaborative role offering a mix of contentious, advisory, and strategic work at the intersection of intellectual property, entertainment, video games, and technology.
What You’ll Be Doing:
Game Protection & Studio Support
Serve as lead legal counsel for SIE’s Game Protection Program in the Americas, developing strategies to combat piracy, respond to pre-release content leaks, and address unauthorized game modifications affecting PlayStation titles.
Partner directly with PlayStation Studios and production, security, and release teams to identify content-protection risks and develop proactive strategies throughout the game development and release lifecycle.
Provide practical and strategic copyright advice, particularly relating to the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), including notice and takedown procedures, counternotices, safe harbors, repeat infringers, fair use, and complex or contested matters.
Advise on emerging and technically complex copyright issues involving game modifications, user-created and unauthorized in-game content, emulators and ports, infringing apps and services, unauthorized distribution, and circumvention of technological protection measures. Help develop practical policies and scalable approaches as these issues evolve across PlayStation Studios and platforms.
Work with investigators, technical and security teams, data specialists, outside counsel, and other partners to develop evidence and translate legal and technical intelligence into effective enforcement action.
IP Enforcement
Support the IP enforcement needs of SIE’s hardware and merchandise businesses in the Americas, developing practical strategies to protect PlayStation products and intellectual property.
Help shape SIE’s broader Americas enforcement strategy, using data and intelligence to identify significant infringers, enforcement gaps, and opportunities for targeted action.
Support anti-counterfeiting efforts across online and physical channels, including marketplace enforcement, investigations, cease-and-desist activity, Customs and border enforcement, administrative and criminal actions, and escalation to litigation or law enforcement when appropriate.
Take an active role in online enforcement across e-commerce marketplaces, social media, websites, apps, and other digital services.
Strategic & Cross-Functional Partnership
Partner with colleagues across SIE’s IP Litigation, Brands, and Patent teams on significant enforcement matters, including strategic litigation and design-related enforcement.
Monitor developments in copyright, intermediary liability, anti-counterfeiting, digital enforcement, and relevant technologies, advising the business on their potential impact.
Develop enforcement policies, playbooks, procedures, and best practices, and provide practical guidance and training to internal stakeholders and external partners.
Use enforcement data and reporting to identify trends, emerging threats, and opportunities to strengthen SIE’s enforcement programs.
Represent SIE, where appropriate, in industry organizations and initiatives relating to copyright, content protection, anti-counterfeiting, and IP enforcement.
Work collaboratively with SIE’s IP Enforcement paralegals in the US and UK, providing legal guidance and supporting their continued development.

A qualified lawyer with approximately
6–12 years of post-qualified experience
in intellectual property enforcement, gained in-house and/or in private practice.
Strong knowledge and practical experience of U.S. copyright law and the DMCA, including online enforcement, notice and takedown processes, counternotices, safe harbors, fair use, and intermediary liability.
Experience developing and executing IP enforcement strategies, ideally involving online enforcement, investigations, anti-counterfeiting, and escalation to litigation or law enforcement.
Experience with, or strong interest in, digital piracy and technically complex copyright matters. Experience involving video games, software, apps, game modifications, circumvention of technological protection measures, or similar digital content issues is particularly valuable.
Strong legal judgment and a pragmatic approach to enforcement, with the ability to prioritize high-impact matters and balance legal risk, enforcement objectives, and commercial considerations.
Ability to work effectively with technical, investigative, and business specialists and translate complex information into practical legal strategies.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the independence and flexibility to operate effectively across regions, cultures, and time zones in a global organization.
Strong technical curiosity and an interest in video games and interactive entertainment, with the ability to understand how games, platforms, and related technologies operate and translate that understanding into practical copyright and enforcement advice.

Experience advising on video games, software, digital content, or other technology products, particularly involving game modifications, emulators, piracy, pre-release content protection, or technological protection measures.
Experience with game or content protection programs, including pre-release leak response, game security, DMCA anti-circumvention, or other technically complex copyright enforcement matters.

jobs.description: An exciting career awaits you At MPC, we’re committed to being a great place to work – one that welcomes new ideas, encourages diverse perspectives, develops our people, and fosters a collaborative team environment. The role serves as the technical focal for GRC automation, developing automated evidence collection, control testing, risk intelligence, and AI-enabled governance capabilities across cloud, on-premises, identity, operational technology (OT), and security platforms. The role collaborates closely with Cyber Fusion, Enterprise Architecture, and Cyber Engineering, to design and build deterministic control-testing logic where deterministic approaches are enough; and AI agents and LLM-backed workflows where reasoning, summarization, or judgment is required, such as evidence-to-control mapping, attestation drafting, drift detection, and audit-package assembly. This position belongs to a family of jobs with increasing responsibility, competency, and skill level. Actual position title and pay grade will be based on the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications. Key Responsibilities Conducts detailed analyses on changes to cybersecurity solutions and its relationship to internal and external systems to assess control effectiveness and cybersecurity risk. Resolves complex multi-functional technical issues. Leverages cybersecurity assessments, standards, control testing methodologies, and compliance frameworks to ensure compliance across security systems. Improves the efficiency and effectiveness of Security solutions, governance processes, automated controls, and monitoring capabilities. Analyzes existing processes and procedures and leads efforts for implementing improvements, automation opportunities, or remediation activities. Responsible for development and submission of Standard Operating Procedures. Analyzes business impacting events, performs initial investigation, and evaluates control performance, exceptions, and risk indicators through continuous monitoring activities. Investigates and analyzes the nature and scope of cyber incidents, control failures, and compliance exceptions. Assists in the development of risk mitigation and remediation plans to ensure regulatory and internal compliance. compliance. Leads implementation of global security initiatives, policies, compliance requirements, and continuous control monitoring practices. Collects, validates, and reports security metrics, control performance results, and remediation efforts associated with them. Manages cyber security-related consulting, guidance, and support to customers and stakeholders. Translates security principles to assist configuration teams with incorporating security and compliance requirements into build and configuration processes. Monitors emerging IT/OT, cybersecurity, automation, and artificial intelligence technologies as well as their impact on the security, risk, and compliance landscape. Education and Experience Bachelor’s Degree in Information Technology, related field or equivalent experience. 5+ years of relevant experience required Experience designing, implementing, and scaling GRC, CCM, or compliance automation solutions within a regulated environment required Experience in Python or comparable automation technologies, proficient in developing, integrating, and supporting automated workflows and REST API-based data integrations across multiple enterprise systems required. Hands-on experience integrating security-control data sources into a GRC / CCM evidence pipeline for continuous control testing required. This includes normalizing API, telemetry, configuration, vulnerability, identity, ticketing, and assessment data into control-level evidence, exception logic, ownership, frequency, and audit-ready records across at least three domains such as CNAPP / CSPM, SIEM / security data lake / XDR, CTEM / VM / ASPM, DSPM, ITSM, IAM, GRC / CCM, or AI/agent governance required. Experience building LLM-backed agentic workflows on Azure AI Foundry, GitHub, or open-source frameworks preferred. Familiarity with NIST AI RMF, the OWASP LLM Top 10, or comparable AI risk frameworks preferred. Skills Adaptability - Maintaining effectiveness when experiencing major changes in work responsibilities or environment (e.g., people, processes, structure, or culture); adjusting effectively to change by exploring the benefits, trying new approaches, and collaborating with others to make the change successful. AI Fundamentals - Understanding of core AI concepts and methods, ability to apply AI to job-relevant use cases and capacity to contribute to organizational AI reimagination. Change Management - Change Management refers to a systematic approach for defining and implementing procedures and/or technologies to deal with changes in the environment. It can mean adapting to change, controlling change and/or effecting change. Authentic Communicator - Expresses ideas and information, both verbally and in writing, clearly and credibly. Listens to understand and fosters constructive dialogue. Cybersecurity Risk Management - The process of developing cyber risk assessment and treatment techniques that can effectively pre-empt and identify significant security loopholes and weaknesses, demonstrating the business risks associated with these loopholes and providing risk treatment and prioritization strategies to effectively address the cyber-related risks, threats and vulnerabilities, ensuring appropriate levels of protection, confidentiality, integrity and privacy in alignment with the security framework. General Programming - Applies a computer language to communicate with computers using a set of instructions and to automate the execution of tasks. Intrusion Detection - The use of security analytics, including the outputs from intelligence analysis, predictive research and root cause analysis in order to search for and detect potential breaches or identify recognized indicators and warnings. Also, monitoring and collating external vulnerability reports for organizational relevance, ensuring that relevant vulnerabilities are rectified through formal change processes. Penetration Testing - The practice of testing a computer system, network or web application to find security vulnerabilities that an attacker could exploit. Penetration testing can be automated with software applications or performed manually. Relationship Management - Relationship Management is the conscious aim to develop and manage long-term and/or trusting relationships with internal or external customers, distributors, suppliers, or other parties in an environment which can include marketing, selling, servicing and other areas where a relationship is crucial to on-going success. jobs.description: Job Description Summary The electrical grid is changing fast — and the engineers who plan high-voltage infrastructure are at the center of that change. As a Lead Primary Design Engineer at GE Vernova, you will take ownership of complex substation design projects across the full voltage spectrum (110kV–380kV), working within international teams to deliver infrastructure that keeps power flowing across On- & Offshore, Air-Insulated Switchgear (AIS) & Gas-Insulated Switchgear (GIS) plants, and renewable energy installations. Your work directly supports the energy transition and the long-term security of supply for grid operators, energy suppliers, and industrial customers. This is a role for someone who sees technical complexity as an opportunity to build something that lasts. Job Description Key Responsibilities Lead the independent development of primary technology solutions for high-voltage projects (110kV–380kV), including floor plans, plant layouts, sections, site plans, construction specifications, mechanical calculations, and remodeling concepts. Own the coordination of constructive interfaces across project workstreams, ensuring alignment between technical design and project delivery requirements. Produce and maintain project documentation using AutoCAD, Primtech, and/or Revit (2D/3D), applying Building Information Modeling (BIM) standards where applicable. Gather and validate required technical plant data and configurations, facilitating interface clarification in coordination meetings with project staff, customers, and suppliers. Communicate clearly within the project team and to management regarding deviations in quality, cost, schedule, and project goals. Contribute as a lead voice in cross-functional project teams, taking responsibility for defined sub-projects from inception through delivery. Qualifications Required A formal education and subsequent Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, with a focus on Energy Technology, is nice to have — we are most interested in your total experience and professional achievements. Significant experience in primary technical planning, project management, and implementation of projects in the high-voltage and extra-high voltage range (110kV–380kV). Proficiency in AutoCAD, Primtech, and/or Revit for 2D/3D design and documentation. Fluent English, with the ability to communicate clearly across international project teams and with external stakeholders. Strong analytical approach and the ability to develop structured, practical solutions to complex technical challenges. Preferred Working knowledge of BIM methodologies and their application in substation design projects. Familiarity with MS Office and Windows in a project engineering environment. Experience coordinating across multi-disciplinary or international project teams. The strongest candidates will bring a track record of leading technical sub-projects in the high-voltage sector, combined with the communication skills to align teams, customers, and suppliers around a shared technical approach. What You'll Find Here: GE Vernova's grid technology teams work on projects that are genuinely varied and technically demanding — from offshore platforms to renewable energy integration. In Katowice, you will be part of an international team that collaborates across borders and disciplines, tackling infrastructure challenges that have real-world consequences for how energy is generated, transmitted, and used. GE Vernova employees rise to the challenge of building a world that works. We provide varied, competitive benefits to help support our workforce — designed to reward strong performance and help you manage your personal and family needs. A healthy, balanced lifestyle means different things to different people, and we've created programs that support the way you live and work today. We also invest in your continued on-the-job learning and development, providing a clear path for career growth.
